avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Induces CYP3A4 and CYP2D6, reducing tamoxifen metabolism and active metabolite (endoxifen) formation, decreasing therapeutic efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; counsel patient to discontinue at least 2 weeks before starting tamoxifen

avoid_supplements.name: Red Clover
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Contains isoflavones with estrogenic activity that may antagonize tamoxifen's therapeutic effects in hormone-sensitive breast cancer
avoid_supplements.action: Contraindicated; recommend alternative botanical support after discussion with oncologist

avoid_supplements.name: Black Cohosh
avoid_supplements.mechanism: May have estrogenic activity and could potentially reduce tamoxifen efficacy in estrogen-dependent cancers
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid or use only under close oncologic supervision; discuss alternatives for menopausal symptom management

avoid_supplements.name: Dong Quai
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Contains phytoestrogens that may compete with tamoxifen at estrogen receptors and reduce therapeutic effect
avoid_supplements.action: Advise against use; explore non-estrogenic alternatives for symptom management

caution_supplements.name: Grapefruit Extract
caution_supplements.mechanism: May inhibit CYP3A4, potentially increasing tamoxifen levels; effect typically modest
caution_supplements.action: Limit intake; monitor for increased side effects (hot flashes, nausea); inform provider if regular consumption occurs

caution_supplements.name: Vitamin E (high-dose >400 IU daily)
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have mild anticoagulant effects; tamoxifen increases thromboembolic risk
caution_supplements.action: Keep doses ≤400 IU daily; monitor for signs of bleeding or clotting

caution_supplements.name: Saw Palmetto
caution_supplements.mechanism: Weak 5-alpha reductase inhibitor; theoretical potential to affect hormone metabolism
caution_supplements.action: Use with caution; not absolutely contraindicated but discuss with oncology team

avoid_foods.name: Grapefruit/Grapefruit Juice
avoid_foods.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibitor that increases tamoxifen blood levels and metabolite concentrations, raising risk of adverse effects
avoid_foods.action: Eliminate grapefruit and juice from diet; switch to alternative citrus fruits (oranges, lemons)

caution_foods.name: High-dose soy products (>25g isoflavones daily)
caution_foods.mechanism: Isoflavones have weak estrogenic activity; excessive intake may theoretically reduce tamoxifen efficacy
caution_foods.action: Moderate consumption acceptable (1-2 servings daily); avoid supplements with concentrated soy isoflavones

caution_foods.name: Cruciferous vegetables (broccoli, cabbage, Brussels sprouts)
caution_foods.mechanism: Contain indole-3-carbinol which may induce estrogen metabolism; excessive amounts theoretically could impact efficacy
caution_foods.action: Normal dietary intake is safe and beneficial; no restriction necessary

monitoring_notes: Monitor for reduced tamoxifen efficacy if CYP2D6 inducing agents are used concomitantly, as conversion to active metabolite endoxifen is critical for therapeutic benefit. Assess adherence and counsel on avoiding estrogenic substances that may compromise cancer treatment outcomes; coordinate with oncology team regarding any supplement use.
